senses.gloss: A document or item put in the same envelope as a letter.
examples: The cover letter lists two *enclosures* at the bottom of the page.
Check the envelope again — the *enclosure* may have slipped out.
Mail the application with all the required *enclosures*.

senses.gloss: A signature written on the back of a check so it can be cashed or deposited.
examples: The bank sent the check back because the *endorsement* was missing.
Write "For deposit only" above your *endorsement*.
Both names have to appear in the *endorsement* on a joint check.

senses.gloss: An official addition to a license, permit, or insurance policy.
examples: You'll need a motorcycle *endorsement* on your driver's license.
We added a flood *endorsement* to the homeowner's policy.
The trucking company pays for the hazmat *endorsement*.

senses.gloss: An arrangement to be somewhere or do something at a set time.
examples: She turned down the dinner because of a prior *engagement*.
The band has three *engagements* lined up this month.
He canceled a speaking *engagement* in Chicago.

senses.gloss: Active involvement in something, or the attention an audience gives it.
examples: The mayor wants more community *engagement* in the planning process.
The post got almost no *engagement* on social media.
Teachers track student *engagement* as closely as test scores.

senses.gloss: A period of fighting between opposing military forces.
examples: The *engagement* lasted less than an hour.
Strict rules of *engagement* limit when troops may fire.
Both ships were damaged in the *engagement*.

senses.gloss: A person who drives a train.
examples: The *engineer* sounded the horn at every crossing.
He spent thirty years as a locomotive *engineer*.
Investigators interviewed the *engineer* after the derailment.

senses.gloss: The very great size or scale of something.
examples: It took a week to grasp the *enormity* of the task ahead.
Standing at the rim, you feel the *enormity* of the canyon.
The *enormity* of the crowd caught the organizers off guard.

senses.gloss: The act of coming into a place, especially a noticeable one.
examples: She made a dramatic *entrance* in a red dress.
The actor missed his *entrance* in the second act.
His *entrance* stopped every conversation in the room.

senses.gloss: Permission or the right to go into a place or join an institution.
examples: *Entrance* to the museum is free on Sundays.
The guard refused us *entrance* without a badge.
She passed the *entrance* exam on her first try.

senses.gloss: The outer limit of what something or someone can do.
examples: The team keeps pushing the *envelope* on battery range.
Test pilots fly right to the edge of the flight *envelope*.
That script pushes the *envelope* of what network TV will air.

senses.gloss: The conditions and surroundings in which someone lives or works.
examples: The office has a relaxed *environment*.
Kids do better in a calm home *environment*.
She quit because of the toxic work *environment*.

senses.gloss: A sudden, widespread outbreak of something harmful other than disease.
examples: The city is dealing with an *epidemic* of car break-ins.
Doctors now call teen loneliness an *epidemic*.
There's an *epidemic* of fake reviews on shopping sites.

senses.gloss: The set of factors that have to be weighed in a situation.
examples: Salary is only one part of the *equation*.
Once kids enter the *equation*, everything changes.
Take emotion out of the *equation* and just look at the numbers.

senses.gloss: A person who enthusiastically promotes a product, idea, or cause.
examples: He's become an *evangelist* for open-source software.
The company hired a developer *evangelist* to speak at conferences.
She's an *evangelist* for biking to work.

senses.gloss: An act of giving one thing and getting another in return.
examples: The two sides agreed to an *exchange* of prisoners.
He fixed my car in *exchange* for a week of dog-sitting.
The treaty allows an *exchange* of scientific data.

senses.gloss: A short conversation or argument between people.
examples: There was a heated *exchange* between the two senators.
I only had a brief *exchange* with her at the door.
The whole *exchange* was caught on video.

senses.gloss: A market where stocks or commodities are bought and sold.
examples: The stock *exchange* closes at four.
The company is listed on two *exchanges*.
Trading was halted on the *exchange* for an hour.

senses.gloss: The carrying out of a plan, or the way something is performed.
examples: The idea was fine; the *execution* was terrible.
The gymnast lost points on *execution*, not difficulty.
Strategy is the easy part — *execution* is what separates them.

senses.gloss: The branch of government that carries out the laws.
examples: The Constitution splits power between the *executive*, the legislature, and the courts.
The court blocked the *executive* from withholding the funds.
Critics argue that the *executive* has grown too powerful.

senses.gloss: The use of a right, power, or ability.
examples: The march was a peaceful *exercise* of free speech.
The veto was a rare *exercise* of presidential power.
Voting is the simplest *exercise* of citizenship.

senses.gloss: A powered frame worn on the body to support or strengthen a person's movements.
examples: The warehouse gave its lifters a powered *exoskeleton* to protect their backs.
A robotic *exoskeleton* helped him walk again after the injury.
The Army is testing *exoskeletons* for soldiers carrying heavy packs.

senses.gloss: The amount of light let into a camera, or a single picture on a roll of film.
examples: A long *exposure* turned the traffic into ribbons of light.
The roll had thirty-six *exposures*.
Bump up the *exposure* a little — the shot is too dark.

senses.gloss: A word or phrase used in a particular way.
examples: "Break a leg" is an old theater *expression*.
I love that *expression* — I'd never heard it before.
Some *expressions* just don't translate.

senses.gloss: The act of putting feelings or ideas into words, art, or action.
examples: The First Amendment protects freedom of *expression*.
The flowers were an *expression* of sympathy.
Dance is her main form of *expression*.

senses.gloss: The family or country a person's ancestors came from.
examples: She's an American of Polish *extraction*.
Half the town is of Norwegian *extraction*.
He's of mixed *extraction* on his mother's side.

senses.gloss: A natural ability to do something easily and well.
examples: She has a real *facility* for languages.
He plays with a *facility* that makes it look effortless.
His *facility* with numbers got him the job.

senses.gloss: A restroom, especially in a public place.
examples: Excuse me — where are the *facilities*?
He asked to use the *facilities* before the drive home.
The rest stop has clean *facilities* and a coffee machine.
